memory_candidates.content: verify-touched.sh on a path with no mapped suite runs a 95-suite 'free' fallback battery and waits on the host gate lock; in a deploy-only repository about 11 agent-system fixture suites fail because agent-system/extensions/ is absent. Give the call a 540s inner timeout and expect that baseline; the result does not depend on the touched file's content.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic derivation proof mode, merged state
sapience_notes.value: Measured on main: 21 tactics, 5 elaborator modules (1,013 lines) in FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode, 8 pure-rule modules (1,157 lines, 624 of them TM-plus copies) in FormalSystem/Theorems/ProofMode, 65 throwError sites, 31 acceptance examples, 2 negative tests with no message assertion, no client outside its own tests.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic proof-mode programme: filed dependency chain
sapience_notes.value: The fourteen filed proof-mode records form one total chain mainly because each edits the same test file, usage guide and two READMEs, not because of logic. Hard dependencies give a spine (scope core and leaf closer, Perpetuity gate, linear-time rules, temporal-slice gate, interface, instances) with side branches. Splitting the shared files and declaring file_scope is the step that makes parallel work possible.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic layer order and the proof mode
sapience_notes.value: FormalSystem/Theorems is layer 2 and Automation and Metalogic are layer 3 (ORGANISATION.md), so pure proof-mode rules can never depend on tactics, proofs under Theorems cannot be written in the mode, and the Minus deduction theorem (Metalogic/Conservativity/MinusDeduction.lean) cannot be used by a rule module under Theorems. A Minus proof-mode instance must sit at layer 3 or the theorem must move down.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic DiscreteUnfolding.unfoldBackward frame class
sapience_notes.value: unfoldBackward is stated at FrameClass.Base; unfoldForward and unfoldBackwardSince are at FrameClass.ZTime. The filed Until/Since proof-mode record says all three are at ZTime, so only two directions need a ZTime certificate.

sapience_notes.subject: BimodalLogic proof-mode interface versus Dense/RTime rules ordering
sapience_notes.value: Decision recorded as open: the interface record says to extract the typeclass after the adequacy tests, which does not require the Dense/RTime rules first. Doing the frame rules after the interface writes them once; doing them before writes TM and TM-plus copies the interface then deletes, but lets the interface see a frame-certificate rule.

sapience_notes.subject: /roadmap and goals documents
sapience_notes.value: The roadmap agent builds its picture from tasks in specs/state.json and reads a goals document only when a quoted instruction names it. Its contract covers adding dependency edges and regrouping batches, not removing edges, so relaxing a sequencing edge is a separate user step.
